subject: Post-call: benchmarking ask + cost sensitivity & cache/batching tests
messages:
From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.com>

Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 14 Aug 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call: benchmarking ask + cost sensitivity & cache/batching tests

Thanks again for the time this morning — good conversation and helpful context on the production traffic profile. Quick recap + proposed next steps so we have alignment before we run the tests.

1) High-level economic comparison (ballpark, normalized to per-1M tokens):
   - Redwood (hosted, conservative mix of gen+context): ~$24 / 1M tokens (includes compute + runtime infra)
   - MegaCloud (hyperscaler A): ~$38 / 1M tokens (good throughput but higher baseline for single-request latency; limited KV/prefix caching options)
   - SkyCompute (hyperscaler B): ~$29 / 1M tokens (discounted CPU path but higher variance on long-context runs)

   Notes: our numbers above include model execution and runtime overhead (network egress and storage tiers excluded). We will finalize exact line-items in the workbook attachment.

2) Key differentiators we discussed:
   - KV/prefix cache + continuous batching to reduce per-token cost for short, repeated prompts (can yield 20-50% unit savings depending on hit rates)
   - Smart routing: fallback to cheaper variant when tail-latency spikes occur
   - Dedicated capacity option for predictable SLA and lower amortized unit cost at scale

3) Proposed tests (we recommend running these next week in a short controlled window):
   A) 1M token short-run (10k requests, avg prompt 30 tokens, avg gen 70 tokens) — measure p50/p95 latency + unit cost
   B) Long-context run (2x context, median completion length increases) — measure tail latencies and cost delta vs A
   C) Cache-hit simulation (synthetic 30% repeated prefix mix) — measure real cache hit rate and effective cost per 1M tokens
   D) Batching sensitivity (batch sizes 1/4/8/16) under our target 500 RPS to quantify throughput vs latency tradeoffs

4) Action items & owners
   - Redwood to provide: test plan + scripts, sandbox API key, initial TCO workbook (attached) — owner: me
   - Acme to provide: representative traffic sample (anonymized) or a short trace we can replay — owner: Leila
   - Joint: schedule a 2-hour run window and a wrap-up sync to review raw logs and the TCO workbook

Attachments: redwood-vs-hyperscaler-cost-model.xlsx, bench-test-plan.md

If that all looks good I can provision the sandbox and we can lock the test window.

Thanks,
Evelyn Hart
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Post-call: benchmarking ask + cost sensitivity & cache/batching tests

Evelyn — thanks for the clear write-up. A few clarifying Qs before we start scheduling:

1) Do the per-1M token numbers include network egress and storage (we have strict S3 policies)? If not, can you provide both: compute-only and total?
2) For the cache-hit numbers, are you assuming cold-start misses when a user first interacts? We typically see ~18-25% prefix reuse in our chat flows today.
3) Can you share the actual scripts you plan to run so our infra team can sign them off (procurement wants to see any load generators up-front)?

cc: procurement@acme-ml.com — can you review the planned test schedule once Evelyn shares scripts?

Carlos
Head of Product
Stratus.ai
